articles.title: We, the Hated review – standing up to be abused: behind the scenes with Just Stop Oil
articles.summary: The levels of violence aimed at these protesters is depressing, but their aim is to save the planet: ‘If they want to destroy everything, they’ve got to go through us’ ‘Hated” is not putting it too strongly.
body: ‘H ated” is not putting it too strongly. The strength of feeling against Just Stop Oil, as caught by this documentary, is really disturbing. It’s filmed from inside the climate group’s protests, and as activists block roads, furious drivers hurl abuse. “Have a wash you fucking idiots!” “Middle class wankers!” It gets physical, too – punching, kicking and dragging. One man appears to drive his van at protesters. Another walks along a line of them, pouring water over their heads, one by one.

Film-maker Rich Felgate could not be closer to the action; his girlfriend, Indigo Rumbelow, is an activist. “Don’t look at the camera. I’m a fly on the wall,” he tells her at their shared house, where books about the suffragettes and Gandhi are on the shelves. On the streets, activists glue themselves to roads and fasten their necks together with bike locks. In October 2022, campaigners notoriously lobbed tomato soup at Van Gogh’s Sunflowers. At one road shutdown an angry driver shouts: “You’re children.” But they’re not all young; a vicar in late middle age with Parkinson’s quickly takes his medicine before he’s cuffed.

articles.title: ‘Tokyo Vice’ Producer, Netflix Executive Urge Changes to Japan’s Production Incentive at MPA Seminar as Government Readies Unified Content Body
articles.summary: “Tokyo Vice” producer Alex Boden and Netflix production policy director Deb Richards urged changes to Japan’s international production incentive at the Motion Picture Association’s annual seminar at the Tokyo International Film Festival, as the government prepares a new body to bring its scattered…
body: He said the minimum spend, raised to JPY800 million ($5.1 million), shut out independent films and co-productions, since most Japanese films cost between $1.5 million and $3 million. He also called for an automatic approval system in place of panel-based selection, which he said made Japan one of the few territories with a subjective incentive, at a time when projects can take three to five years to come together.

“So how does a producer know that they can count on the Japan incentive in advance? That’s the question, and we need a solution,” Boden said. He pointed to Martin Scorsese’s “Silence,” “Pachinko” and “Shōgun” as Japan-set projects that scouted in the country but shot elsewhere, and argued for building training into the incentive, citing the U.K.’s 0.5% ScreenSkills levy as a model.

“You can have a lower incentive, that’s fine, as long as it’s certain, as long as the criteria are clear,” Richards said during the panel. “And that’s one of the things that for the Japan incentive, the criteria is not clear.” She added that applicants could work out why they were turned down only by looking at who was approved, calling the process “opaque.”

articles.title: Netflix Docuseries ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ Is a Tragic, Mournful Portrait of Addiction: TV Review
articles.summary: There are not a lot of famous people in “The One About Matthew Perry.” None of the late actor’s “Friends” castmates sat for an interview for the three-part Netflix docuseries; neither did Perry’s longtime friend and “Simpsons” star Hank Azaria, who knew Perry as a striving young actor in L.A., or…
body: “God, you can do anything you want to me; just please make me famous,” Perry freely admits to praying in his youth. (He got “Friends” shortly afterward, but ruefully notes that “God didn’t forget” about the first part.) “The One About Matthew Perry” is more a collation of established facts about Perry’s battles, including a sepsis-induced coma in 2018 resulting from his use of opiates, and an unveiling of new ones. What the project adds are personal testimonies about witnessing said battles up close, plus memorable observations like “intimacy was his greatest fear and his greatest wish.” Though the most memorable lines — “Reality is an acquired taste,” say — fittingly belong to Perry.
All three episodes of “The One About Matthew Perry” are now streaming on Netflix.

articles.title: City of Masks review – theatreland ghost story with female phantom of the opera out for revenge
articles.summary: In a West End theatre, a young actor hears a disembodied voice coaching his singing. It’s the start of an icky ghost-on-human romance. This ghost story set in a West End theatre is creakier than the old wooden floorboards on stage.
body: Victor is suspected of involvement in the fire that killed Eve and the tabloids are sniffing around. Meanwhile, Eve is all out for revenge: lights flicker, bits of rigging fly off the walls. Whether or not she is a ghost, Christian seems to be developing big feelings for her – and as in any film with the prospect of ghost-on-human romance, it gets a bit ick. And as it goes on the film gets more and more baffling, so confusing that I went back and watched it again, convinced I’d missed something vital that would make sense of it. But no.

articles.title: Sir Tom Jones 'truly sorry' as he cancels two shows due to illness
articles.summary: Sir Tom has pushed back two concerts in the US on doctor's advice, due to "a bad case of the flu".
body: Sir Tom Jones said he is "truly sorry" after rescheduling two forthcoming concerts due to "a bad case of the flu".
The 86-year-old singer from Pontypridd, Rhondda Cynon Taf, is currently on his Come Gather Round world tour.
He announced the decision to push back his Monday show in Los Angeles, and Tuesday's concert in San Diego, following doctor's advice.
In a post on Instagram, he wrote: "Following doctor's advice, I unfortunately have to reschedule tonight's show in Los Angeles and tomorrow's show in San Diego."

articles.title: Donnie Iris, Pittsburgh’s Favorite Rocker, Who Scored Hits With the Jaggerz and as a Solo Artist, Dies at 83
articles.summary: Donnie Iris, regarded as Pittsburgh’s biggest hometown rock hero for a six-decade career that included hit singles in the 1960s and ’80s, died Monday at 83. He had been fighting bladder cancer for three years. Iris’ biggest chart success came as a member of the Jaggerz, who reached No.
body: That group petered out, but he went on to have continued success, especially regionally, as the frontman of Donnie Iris and the Cruisers in the age of power pop and Midwest rock. A decade after “The Rapper” broke through, Iris had a hit again with “Ah! Leah!,” which reached No. 29 on the Hot 100 in 1980. They had two more mid-level chart hits in 1981 with “Love Is Like a Rock” and “My Girl.”

His modest success during that era on the Billboard charts was hardly indicative of just how beloved he was in his native Pennsylvania and the Midwest region, widely seen as being to Pittsburgh what Michael Stanley was to Cleveland.

“For my money, he was the most beloved Pittsburgh musician of all time,” Joe Grushecky told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. Grushecky, as the leader of the Iron City Houserockers, would have been one of the few other viable candidates for that title. But, as he told the newspaper, “I don’t know anyone who was loved more than Donnie. He just had that warmth about him, and it came through in his performance.”

articles.title: ‘Mirzapur’ Tops a Decade of Indian Streaming as New Commissions Fall, IMDb Report Finds (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Viewer interest in Indian shows on IMDb rose about 17-fold over the past decade, even as the number of new shows and seasons commissioned in the country has dropped for two straight years, according to a new IMDb study that traces the growth of Indian streaming through its most popular titles.
body: “ Mirzapur ” led the pack with nine appearances, having made the list every year since it launched. “Scam 1992” was the only show to chart five times off a single season.
Crime and thriller titles took 48 of the 110 positions. In the later years, horror, romance, comedy and drama all made gains.

Among streamers, Prime Video and Amazon MX Player combined for 34 positions across 17 series, more than any other service. Netflix logged 21 positions spread over 18 series, the broadest range of distinct titles of the platforms the report examined.

YouTube emerged as a launchpad. Thirteen of the 64 charting series started life there, and 11 of those were later picked up by subscription services. The report credited the platform with giving a wide base of creators room to build stories that can travel to bigger audiences.

articles.title: 'A way to escape': Fan excitement as new ACOTAR book hits shelves
articles.summary: About 40 fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses series celebrated at a "lock-in" event in Carrickfergus.
body: Torrential rain and high winds may not be what many would consider fantastical.
But it didn't stop about 30 hardcore fans turning out for the latest release of author Sarah J Maas’ romantasy series, A Court of Splintered Harmony, in Carrickfergus, County Antrim.
The sixth book in Maas's multi-million book selling series, A Court of Thorns and Roses (ACOTAR), was released at midnight on Tuesday after a five-year wait.
On Monday evening, a midnight release event was held in The Secret Bookshelf, an independent bookshop just off the town's main street.

articles.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
articles.summary: The rapper has been involved with the show for years but has never before performed at the NFL championship game.
body: Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show in February, the NFL has announced.
Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the half-time show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer but he has not performed before at the NFL championship game.
"Anticipation as to who Jay-Z might have guest star at halftime for the big game will now kick off," the NFL said in a statement. "Of course, his wife, Beyoncé, will be atop the list."
Next year's Super Bowl LXI will take place on 14 February near Los Angeles.

articles.title: ‘The Terminal List’ Star Breaks Down the Season 2 Finale’s Intense Action and What’s Next for Raife
articles.summary: Tom Hopper discusses The Terminal List Season 2, Raife Hasting's bond with James Reece, the intense finale action, and his hope to tackle Savage Son.
body: Editor's note: The following contains major spoilers for The Terminal List Season 2.

In Season 2 of the Prime Video series The Terminal List, based on former Navy SEAL-turned-author Jack Carr 's second novel True Believer, former Navy SEAL operative Raife Hastings ( Tom Hopper ) discovers weapons shipments that have ended up in the hands of terrorists and teams up with investigative journalist Katie Buranek ( Constance Wu ) to get answers. As trust between them grows and they face threats together, they realize that their mission intersects with what Navy SEAL Commander James Reece ( Chris Pratt ) is dealing with. Eventually, Raife meets up with Reece so that they can stop a conspiracy with roots running back to Reece’s own Navy SEAL father.
COLLIDER: Because of how real this show feels, it always raises my anxiety level while watching it.

articles.title: Meghan to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia
articles.summary: The Duchess of Sussex says she "can't wait" to take part in the programme, which will air next year.
body: The Duchess of Sussex has been confirmed as a co-host of the new season of Junior MasterChef Australia.
Meghan will join the 2027 series as a "special guest" with fellow host Poh Ling Yeow, according to Australia's Channel 10.

The duchess said she "can't wait" to take part in the programme after an appearance as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia last year. It was the show's largest Sunday audience since 2023, according to the statement from Paramount ANZ.
The announcement comes as Meghan faces increased scrutiny due to her father Thomas Markle being accused of child sexual abuse. He denies the allegations.
